 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 164 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that: On 14-09-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., Harish.T.D was driving Ford Fiesta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AB-9823 from Tiptur side towards Tarabenahalli and when he reached near Lingadahalli Gate, Tiptur-Hassan Road, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time Harish T D lost control over the vehicle and dashed to a Uculyptus Tree which was on the right side of the footpath, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc.
3.
The respondent No.3 is the wife and respondent No.4 is the son of the deceased.
4. Prior to the accident, Harish.T.D was hale and healthy.
He was Agriculturist and earning sum of Rs.3,300/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of Harish T D, petitioners and respondent no.3 and 4 have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages.

5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Ford Fiesta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AB-9823 and the respondent no.3 and 4 are the wife and son of Harish T D have remained absent.

Hence they were placed ex-parte.
6.

The respondent 2 and 5/ the Insurer of Ford Fiesta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AB-9823 have filed written statement and admitted that they have issued a Liability only policy to the car bearing No.KA-05-AB- 9823 .

The respondent no.2 and 5 have contended that the policy does not cover the risk of the driver and Harish T D being a driver of the Car was not covered, that the insured car was not involved in the accident and that T D Harish being the tort feasor, the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation under the provisions of MV Act.

The respondent no.2 and 5 further contended that in the present case only one vehicle was involved and death was caused on account of the own act of rashness and negligence, in this regard the charge sheet is filed against Harish T D and as such the claim petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable and that Harish T D was driving the car without having a valid and effective driving license.

7. On the basis of rival pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:

Hence, issue no 2 is answered in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, deceased was driving Ford Fiesta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AB-9823 from Tiptur side towards Tarabenahalli and when he reached near Lingadahalli Gate, Tiptur-Hassan Road, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk,

sentences.text: In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the father of deceased got examined himself as Pw1 and produced in all 13 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.10 are the police documents i.e., F.I.R, Complaint, Spot sketch, Spot mahazar, photographs of the spot, IMV reports, Inquest, Post Mortem report, death certificate and charge sheet, etc., which are the material documents to prove the present issue.

15. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the wife of the deceased by name Shobha, case has been registered against the deceased in Crime No.0090/2023 of Tiputur Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 279 & 304A of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the deceased for the offence punishable under Sections 279 & 304A of IPC.
16.

The respondent no. 2 and 5 in their written statement and evidence have categorically contended that the accident in question was due to the sole negligence of the deceased and deceased being the tortfeasor the petitioners cannot claim compensation under the provisions of MV Act.

It is further submitted that the liability to pay compensation to the person who has suffered injury or to the legal heirs of the victim is envisaged only in cases where such injury or death was caused because of a tortuous act committed by another.
In the present case since only one vehicle was involved and death was caused on account of the own negligence of the deceased, the claim petition is not maintainable.

17. So far as the objection raised by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 and 5 regarding the maintainability of the petition on the ground that the deceased himself was the tortfeasor is concerned, It is not in dispute that petitioners have filed this petition u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
If the claim petition is filed u/Sec.164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the injured person.

18. In a decision reported in ILR 2008 KAR 1249 in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Salma and others Hon'ble lordships have held that:
"a petition under section163A of the act is maintainable even in case where negligence is on the part of the victim"

"Section 163A also covers the cases where negligence is even on the part part of the victim held excluding the defense of contributory negligence".

It is was held that "In a petition u/Sec. 163 -A of MV Act the question as to who was riding the vehicle or who was responsible for the accident or the relationship of the victim in relation to the motor vehicle and its owner become completely irrelevant.

21. In MFA No. 3551/2011 (MV) decided on 20- 09-2021 between Sri Ashok K Vs., Sri Karthik &
Anr., In the said case also claim petition was filed u/Sec. 163- A MV Act. As like in the present case,
the insurer has taken the contention that the victim suffered injuries due to his own negligence when he was riding his own motorcycle therefore claim petition u/Sec. 163- A of the Act is not maintainable.

22. In MFA No. 3889/2011 (MV-D) decided on 11-06-2019 between Smt. Priya & Ors., Vs. Sri Armugam & Anr.,

entities.text: Smt. Priya & Ors., Vs. Sri Armugam & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, claim petition was filed u/Sec. 163-A of the MV Act.
In the said case also the deceased skidded from the motorcycle and succumbed to the injuries.
The Insurance company has taken contention that the accident took place due to the own negligence of the deceased.
Hence, claim petition is not maintainable.
In the said case, it was held that "the principle of strict liability has been incorporated under Section 163A of the Act.

Therefore, even in a case where there is no tortfeasor and no negligence caused by any tort feasor, but on account of the use of the motor vehicle in a public place, an injury or death is caused, in such a situation under Section 163A of the Act read with Second Schedule, on structured formula basis, the claim petition would have to be considered dehors the aspect of negligence.

23. The learned counsel in further has referred the judgment rendered in MFA No. 4886/2011, 2007 ACJ 278, ILR 2008 KAR 1249, 2018 ACJ 1 (SC) ,
24. wherein it was held that Insurance company is not permitted to raise a defence of negligence when petition is filed u/Sec. 163-A of the MV Act.
Compensation u/Sec. 163-A can be awarded to the claimant even if he himself is negligent.

25. In view of the above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 164 of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered is whether vehicle against which the claim is made is involved in the accident.
In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Respondents have denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

26. Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P10, this court is of the opinion that the accident was due to the involvement or use of the offending vehicle and in that the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

6 27. Issue No.3:-

entities.text: Dharma T H vs Younus Khan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly this petition is filed u/Sec.164 of IMV Act.

Sec. 164 of MV Act reads as follows:
"164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc.-

(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section".
28.
As per Sec.164 of MV Act petitioners are entitled for fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
29. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2 nd and 5th respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the deceased who was the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident was holding valid driving license.

But the learned counsel for respondent 2 and 5 have disputed their liability to pay the compensation on the ground that the policy issued by the respondent no.2 and 5 in respect of the vehicle in question is 'Act Only policy' which come under statutory liability.
Under statutory liability only the risk of 3rd party would cover but not the driver.
Further in the present case only 3rd party premium is paid and no additional premium was paid to cover the risk of the driver.
30. Per contra, it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for the petitioners by referring the head "DRIVER' in the Insurance policy.
That the policy covers even the risk of the driver of the said vehicle ie., the risk of the deceased.

31. If Ex.R2 and Ex.R6 is perused, under the head DRIVER it is stated that "Any person including the insured: Provided that a person driving holds an effective driving licence at the time of the accident and is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.

Provided also that the person holding an effective Learner's licence may also drive the vehicle and that such a person satisfies the requirements of Rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989".
32.
In an Act only (Third Party liability) in the Insurance Policy certificate the driver column indicates the persons legally permitted to drive the Insured vehicle for the policy to remain valid.

Dharma T H vs Younus Khan on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51359565/
7

entities.text: Dharma T H vs Younus Khan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The driver column does not indicate that under 'Act Only Policy' it covers the risk even of the driver.
Further no additional premium is seen to be a paid, so as to cover the risk of the driver.
33. Claim for the driver's risk under an "Act Only Policy" filed u/Sec. 164 of the MV Act is not covered as the policy is limited to third party liability only.
34. Sec.164 claims are for no fault compensation for the death or injury from an accident, but this liability is limited to third party risk.
A claim for the driver's own injury or death would require a comprehensive or package policy which includes personal accident cover for the owner-driver.

In Civil Appeal No. .... of 2025 @ SLP (c) No. 5885/2019 between Manjusha & Ors., Vs., United Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr., In the said case, in the beginning para the question was raised whether the family of the brother of the owner of the vehicle who died in the accident when the tyre of the car he was driving burst is entitled to claim compensation under the MV Act.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No. .... of 2025 @ SLP (c) No. 5885/2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Manjusha & Ors., Vs., United Insurance Co.Ltd., & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held "it is trite that the insurer has no statutory liability to cover the risk of the owner or the driver of the vehicle who steps into the shoes of the owner, when the statutory liability is restricted to third party liabilities.

35. In Ramkhiladi Vs. United India Insurance Co., (2020) 2 SCC 550 in which the petition was filed u/Sec.163-A of the Act wherein it was held that "the borrower of a vehicle who was driving cannot raise a claim under no fault liability since the driver of the vehicle steps into the shoes of the owner".

entities.text: Ramkhiladi Vs. United India Insurance Co., (2020) 2 SCC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
36. Further in a judgment referred by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 reported in 2009 AIR SCW 4916 between Ningamma & Anr., Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd., In the said case,
deceased driving motorcycle after borrowing it from real owner.

entities.text: 2009 AIR SCW 4916 between Ningamma & Anr., Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus he stepped into shoes of the owner of vehicle.
Hence, Lrs of deceased could not claim compensation u/Sec. 163- A of the Act.

37. By considering the observation made in the aforesaid judgment coupled with the fact that the policy issued to the vehicle in question is 'Act Only Policy' which covers the risk only of third party and deceased being the driver of the vehicle, his risk does not cover under the said policy, hence the claimants are not entitled for compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly issue no 3 is answered in the Negative.
38. Issue No.4 :- In the light of the findings given on issue no. 1 to issue no.3, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.

Further no additional premium is seen to be a paid, so as to cover the risk of the driver.
33. Claim for the driver's risk under an "Act Only Policy" filed u/Sec. 164 of the MV Act is not covered as the policy is limited to third party liability only.
34. Sec.164 claims are for no fault compensation for the death or injury from an accident, but this liability is limited to third party risk.
A claim for the driver's own injury or death would require a comprehensive or package policy which includes personal accident cover for the owner-driver.
36. Further in a judgment referred by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 reported in 2009 AIR SCW 4916 between Ningamma & Anr., Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd., In the said case,
deceased driving motorcycle after borrowing it from real owner.
37. By considering the observation made in the aforesaid judgment coupled with the fact that the policy issued to the vehicle in question is 'Act Only Policy' which covers the risk only of third party and deceased being the driver of the vehicle, his risk does not cover under the said policy, hence the claimants are not entitled for compensation from the respondents.

It is further submitted that the liability to pay compensation to the person who has suffered injury or to the legal heirs of the victim is envisaged only in cases where such injury or death was caused because of a tortuous act committed by another.
Further the learned counsel for petitioners has referred the judgment rendered in MFA No.
1292/2010 decided on 27-07-2022 between Sri L Mallesh & Ors., Vs. Sri Krupa Rao.
23. The learned counsel in further has referred the judgment rendered in MFA No. 4886/2011, 2007 ACJ 278, ILR 2008 KAR 1249, 2018 ACJ 1 (SC) ,
24. wherein it was held that Insurance company is not permitted to raise a defence of negligence when petition is filed u/Sec. 163-A of the MV Act.
